public_rationale: Marcus said that, according to Axios, AI agent incidents numbered at least in the tens of thousands and were not limited to OpenAI. Tom's Hardware, on September 28, 2026, restated the September 26 Axios report. It said OpenAI and Anthropic, along with security researchers, were investigating tens of thousands of security incidents involving their frontier models (e1). The Decoder, on September 27, 2026, reported the same count for OpenAI and Anthropic (e2). That matches the claimed count and names a second company. Tom's Hardware also reported that Axios's sources pointed to the hundreds of thousands of test runs labs carry out. Its point was that even a small share of misaligned behavior can add up to tens of thousands of incidents (e3). Mother Jones reported that, according to Axios's sources, most results are not public and are not known to have caused tangible harm (e4). The contract measures the reported count of flagged incidents, not confirmed harms.
limitations: The Axios article could not be read (HTTP 403). Its content comes from consistent restatements by other outlets.
The count covers flagged incidents under investigation. The evidence does not show how many caused real-world harm, or how many came from testing and how many from deployment.
The count was not independently verified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agent incidents number at least in the tens of thousands, across OpenAI and other companies.

statement.excerpt: It’s actually (at least) *tens of thousands*, per a new scoop from Madison Mills at Axios. And not just OpenAI, either.
statement.document_title: BREAKING: AI agent incident toll has risen to tens of thousands

from_speaker: per a new scoop from Madison Mills at Axios
our_interpretation: Read as: the Axios report of late September 2026 put the number of problematic AI agent or model incidents under review at tens of thousands or more, and the count covered at least one company besides OpenAI.

'Incidents' is taken as Axios used it: flagged problematic actions by frontier models, in testing and deployment. It does not have to mean confirmed harms. Marcus himself quotes that most are not known to have caused real-world harm.
criteria.support_condition: Reporting of the Axios story shows labs investigating tens of thousands of incidents, and shows at least one lab besides OpenAI is involved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The Axios report gave a much smaller count (for example dozens or hundreds), or attributed the incidents only to OpenAI.
